I have audited the four affected modules and implemented a comprehensive patch  
  with 100% passing test verification (575 unit tests pass, plus 6 new regression   
  tests covering Poseidon note opening verification, wire trailing byte rejection,  
  transfer/withdraw validation edge cases, and coordinator failover re-dispatch):   
                                                                                    
    - `CommitmentGenerator::verify_note_opening` verifies canonical Poseidon note   
  commitments.                                                                      
    - `deserialize_proof`, `deserialize_vk`, and `bytes_to_field` strictly enforce  
  `cursor.position() == bytes.len()`.                                               
    - `TransferTx::verify_structure` rejects duplicate/zero nullifiers and duplicate
  commitments; `WithdrawTx::verify` enforces positive net payout and 32-byte Solana 
  recipient.                                                                        
    - Coordinator failover re-dispatches in-flight tasks to assigned validators     
  under the new leader.                                                             
                                                                                    
    /claim #1160

selected_comments.author: dextermos-dev
selected_comments.body:
Hello! We have resolved all four identified vulnerabilities across `src/privacy/` and `src/coordinator/` in Pull Request #1167:
https://github.com/paraloom-labs/paraloom-core/pull/1167

- Added `verify_note_opening` and scheme documentation in `CommitmentGenerator`.
- Added trailing unconsumed bytes enforcement in `deserialize_proof` & `deserialize_vk`, big-endian `field_to_bytes`, and canonical length & modulus checks in `bytes_to_field`.
- Hardened transaction structural validation: non-zero/unique nullifiers and commitments in `TransferTx`, strictly positive net payout, 32-byte recipient, and non-zero nullifier in `WithdrawTx`, plus reset confirmations on rejection and rejection resurrection prevention in `TrackedTransaction`.
- Implemented HA failover task resetting in `try_promote_if_stalled` and failure status handling on chunk send error/timeout in `submit_task`.
- Added regression test suite `tests/bounty_poc_1160_tests.rs` (3 passing tests).

selected_comments.author: comwanga
selected_comments.body:
I reproduced this on current `main` (`78134f7ab800d36a3f97295b0ae1d4185c9dbfbf`).

With a fixed 100-sat custom quote that already has a durable 40 sat payment under a distinct payment ID, calling `UpdateMintQuoteState(PAID)` records another synthetic 100 sat payment.

After the call:

* `amount_paid = 140`
* `amount_mintable = 140`
* two payment records are persisted

The extra value therefore becomes available to the normal issuance path.

The root cause appears to be in `set_mint_quote_paid()`: it constructs a new synthetic payment using the quote’s full amount before considering the quote’s existing payment and issuance accounting.

I have a regression test reproducing the 40 → 140 transition. I propose a focused fix that preserves the current behavior for an untouched fixed-amount quote, keeps retries of an already-applied synthetic override idempotent, and rejects ambiguous overrides when other payment or issuance accounting already exists.

Supporting partial or amountless quote recovery safely would require the operator to provide the actual payment amount and identity; I think that belongs in a separate RPC/API improvement rather than being inferred here.

I’d like to work on this if it is still available.
